candidates.title: Capture and qualify incoming leads

demandEvidence.chore: Capture and qualify incoming leads in a workflow.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I built a lead capture and qualification workflow in n8n using Apollo, OpenAI, Airtable, Slack, and Gmail.

ease.reason: A synthetic lead row can be labeled for review, but no supplied implementation reference documents these integrations.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional service firms might pay for lead qualification; this maker build does not establish external demand or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can label fictional lead rows and prepare a review queue; integrations and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed intake and qualification loop could repeat, while a person verifies fit and follow-up; implementation is undocumented.

evidence.reason: The post reports a lead-capture and qualification workflow, but does not establish an unmet chore, frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: this is a maker build report rather than an external request; a synthetic qualification mock is possible, but demand and implementation support are absent.

candidates.title: Recover access to existing workflows

demandEvidence.chore: Recover access to the owner account and make existing workflows visible without losing them.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How do I recover access to the original owner account / make my existing workflows visible again without losing them?

ease.reason: A student could draft a generic recovery checklist, but no supplied reference documents a safe platform procedure.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: workflow consultants might pay for recovery help; this one-off request proves no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A fictional checklist is possible, but account ownership, platform access and data preservation are unresolved.

autonomy.reason: Recovery requires an authorized administrator and careful human control; no safe unattended loop is supported.

evidence.reason: The request clearly asks to restore owner access and workflow visibility, but supplies no procedure, recurrence or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: this is a one-off, sensitive account-recovery request; safe access and workflow preservation are undocumented and human-dependent.

candidates.title: Draft updates from changing order data

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare customer-facing status updates when operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d be interested to hear how others handle customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.

ease.reason: Synthetic order rows could test a draft, but no supplied implementation reference supports a store connection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops may pay for clearer order updates; the discussion proves neither payment nor a service market.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft from synthetic status changes; live store access and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop can prepare drafts, but a person must verify changing facts and approve messages; implementation is undocumented.

evidence.reason: The post asks about customer-facing updates when operations data is incomplete or changing, but gives no frequency or fields.

candidates.reason: Below threshold and duplicate of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 on the ecommerce customer and customer-communication workflow.

candidates.title: Prepare a restaurant order arrival alert

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare an alert when a restaurant website receives an order.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A mock can format an operator-supplied test order, but no supplied reference supports the website trigger or WhatsApp delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small restaurants may pay for timely order alerts; the request establishes neither market demand nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can format synthetic orders into alert text; live website access and messaging delivery are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop formats each supplied order, but trigger and delivery are unsupported and a person must verify alerts.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly seeks automated restaurant order notifications, but gives no frequency, fields or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the concrete alert idea is assessable with synthetic orders, but trigger and delivery capability have no supplied implementation evidence.
